condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is 1-phenyl-2,3-dimethyl-5-pyrazolone (antipyrine); the closest supplied structural analog pirfenidone is reported as rapidly absorbed with high oral bioavailability (C12) and has 46% absolute oral bioavailability in rats (C31), both above the 20% threshold.

L3 fasted oral-exposure records for pirfenidone show rapid fasted absorption (median Tmax 0.5 h, C41) and substantial plasma AUC/Cmax after oral dosing (C46, C50, C43), consistent with meaningful oral bioavailability.

L4 intestinal-absorption records show complete or near-complete human absorption for related small lipophilic drugs, including phenylbutazone (C57), diazepam (C51, C59, C61), and ketoprofen (C52, C55, C58, C60, C62); phenylbutazone shares the pyrazolone/pyrazolidinedione core.

L5 gut-wall records show very high permeability for edaravone (C72), a closely related pyrazolone, and high Papp with efflux ratios near 1 for other small heterocycles (C68, C64, C66, C67, C73, C71), indicating no gut-wall efflux barrier.

L6 hepatic-clearance records are predominantly for mephenytoin CYP2C19 variants (C75, C76, C78, C79, C80, C82, C84, C86), diazepam (C77), meperidine (C81), and mephenytoin under hypoxia (C85); C83 measures Norantipyrine CLint in human liver microsomes, a metabolite, not parent antipyrine first-pass loss. None provides affirmative evidence of F < 20% for the query.
No affirmative evidence supports F < 20%; the lowest relevant values in the supplied contexts (teneligliptin 43%, pirfenidone rat 46%, ondansetron under rifampin 40%) remain above threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct measured absolute oral bioavailability for the query molecule itself is present in the supplied records.
No query-specific IV-comparator or human F study is provided; fasted inference relies on structural analogs and absence of food-dependent liabilities.
L6 hepatic-clearance records are mostly for other molecules; C83 measures a metabolite (Norantipyrine), not parent antipyrine first-pass clearance.
Pirfenidone's human absolute oral bioavailability has not been determined (C24); its human 'high' value is qualitative, and the rat value is 46%.
No query-specific intestinal metabolism or first-pass clearance data are available.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high: F >= 20% remains well supported by close structural analog pirfenidone (high oral bioavailability; rat F 46%), complete intestinal absorption for related pyrazolone/pyrazolidinedione drugs, and L5 gut-wall permeability/efflux records showing high permeability and no efflux barrier; L6 hepatic-clearance records do not provide affirmative evidence of low F for antipyrine, so the high prediction is kept.
